Header: Fusarium oxyporum f.sp. Kajoor ka Murjhao

Prevention: Fusarium oxyporum is a fungus that is spread through mechanical means.
The most common ways plants are infected is from contaminated purchased trees and unsanitary pruning practices.
Use clean, disease-free palms for planting.
Provide supplemental water and clean up infected debris immediately.
Do not compost infected material, as spores can still survive and infest your compost heap.
Disinfect tools with one part bleach in four parts water or with 70% rubbing alcohol (isopropyl).
Avoid movement of soil and runoff water so as to not spread the disease.
Leave infected soil to fallow or rotate with other crops for 3 years.
Monitoring: The symptoms usually start at the lower or older fronds (leaves) and move up the palm.
Drying begins terminal part to cover the whole frond and turns to pale brown and the tree dies within a few months.
The disease does the most damage in plants that are in dry regions.
Direct Control: Prune off dying fronds but disinfect tools before using them on other plants.
Restrictions: There are no cures for this disease.
Fungicides have been evaluated, but none have been effective.
Disease management is based solely on disease prevention.
